LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 3.3.1 PRONOUNS (‘I, YOU’)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Language use 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’), part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Which words do you use to talk about yourself?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner signs engagingly as they use facts and examples to support their own opinion in a conversation

using the pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you’.

• Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital technology as they record a conversation between family members using the pronouns ‘I’

and ‘you’ during a role play.

Values:
Love: Compassion is enriched as the learner understands and appreciates the other’s opinions as they work together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: self-esteem is nurtured as the learner uses the pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you ‘to talk about and sign members of the family.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Concepts of pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you’ are learnt in Kiswahili and Kenya Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resources

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings
